West Virginia has two mapped data center facilities and zero recorded megawatts of capacity, making it one of the lightest-footprint states in the national data center landscape.

The two facilities, Morgan Wireless in Bath and Alpha Federal in South Charleston, are small enough that no power draw has been captured in this dataset. That absence matters: total megawatts are the figure that connects a facility to grid load, and without it the state cannot be evaluated as a potential node in AI compute infrastructure. Small regional facilities of this kind typically serve local connectivity or government functions rather than the dense GPU clusters that drive AI training workloads.

What the data does not cover is whether either facility has expansion plans, available land, or transmission access, all of which would be relevant to any assessment of West Virginia's future role. The two-facility count and zero-megawatt figure describe the current recorded state only.
